key_insight: Accurate tumor-growth predictions can still come from the wrong law, so symbolic discovery must be judged by mathematical validity and law recovery, not just fit quality.
engineering_relevance: For computational modeling workflows, the paper shows that coefficient refitting and candidate ranking can materially change which equations are selected, affecting downstream reliability in data-driven scientific discovery.
method: Generate sparse/noisy synthetic Gompertz tumor-growth data and compare recovered laws to the known truth.
Apply symbolic regression, admissibility screening, coefficient refitting, and LLM-based ranking to shortlist candidate equations.
Evaluate trajectory fit, forecasting, and governing-law recovery separately.
evidence_signal: On synthetic data, dense noiseless sampling recovered the true family, while sparse noisy sampling often produced alternative forms; classical nonlinear least squares usually improved law error, but PINN refitting often worsened it.
watch_item: LLM rankings and fit-based selection can favor plausible-looking but mathematically incorrect laws, so human-checkable admissibility and independent law-recovery metrics are needed.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
